{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less: build it and its tests yourself, then have the testing section probe it, fix what it finds and run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake testing to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line) and near-miss copies of the key functions (one plausible bug each). Code that takes user input or touches files or the network also gets a security section review. Then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no other builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder, testing for tests, near-miss copies and final verification, the security section for a security pass before the final review (the one cross-review you ask for), and the docs section always. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs, the security pass and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). Pass: overall at least 9 and no item under 7.
- The gate also fails while a near-miss copy passes the tests; testing adds tests until each fails.
- Near-miss copies live only in `.team/near-miss/` and stay there; swap one in only after every builder has reported, and always restore the original.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 3 fix rounds. Then report the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 3 fix rounds here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the near-miss check).

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Max mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.name: heapdump

commands.name: init

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec

commands.name: reload-plugins

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: ultrareview
commands.description: Start a cloud agent that finds and verifies bugs in your branch (~5-15 min, $5-$25 USD) · Runs in a cloud session. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage

commands.name: recap

commands.name: skill-doctor
commands.description: Show which loaded skills are unused and costing context

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

# Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02

AUTOMATED BENCHMARK TASK. No human will answer questions: the requirements below are complete and final. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. The project's own tests must pass at the end.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `

... [5984 characters truncated] ...

 (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.
- Rooms: the HTML holds no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.

- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

# Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02

AUTOMATED BENCHMARK TASK. No human will answer questions: the requirements below are complete and final. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. The project's own tests must pass at the end.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `

... [5893 characters truncated] ...

dy cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.
- Rooms: the HTML holds no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage.

input.content:
# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. `server.mjs` is one HTTP server that serves a JSON API and a browser page. You can book three fixed rooms (`Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`) by date and time, list and filter bookings, and cancel them. All data is kept in one JSON file.

## Requirements

- Node.js (a version with `node:test`, 18 or later).
- No dependencies. You do not need to run `npm install`.

## Usage

```sh
npm start            # same as: node server.mjs
```

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is ready it prints one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a browser (use the port from that line).

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means 3000. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick any free port, and the startup line shows which one. It must be ASCII digits only and no more than 65535. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

Example:

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=data/b.json node server.mjs
```

The server never creates folders, so `data/` must already exist. If it does not, the server still starts, but every booking or cancel fails with `500 internal error`.

On startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening. If `PORT` is invalid or the port cannot be bound (for example because it is already in use), the server writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1.

## Data file

- The file holds `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [...]}`.
- It is read once, at startup:
  - If it does not exist, the server starts with no bookings.
  - If it cannot be read for any other reason (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not valid data, the server prints `cannot read data file <name>` to stderr and exits with code 1.
- After startup the server's memory is the source of truth. Edits made to the file while the server runs are not noticed.
- The file is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and always before the reply is sent. After a restart you get the same bookings and the same next id.
- Ids start at 1 and are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.

## API

Every JSON reply has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": "<message>"}`.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

| Method & path | Success | Errors |
|---------------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above) | |
| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200, with only the bookings on that date | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` (an empty value counts as invalid) |
| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 with the new booking | see the validation rules below |
| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found` (the id is unknown, or is not a positive integer without a leading zero) |
| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |

Errors that apply to every route:

- Any other path: 404 `not found`. This includes `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`.
- A known path with a method it does not support (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example, `GET /api/bookings/abc` returns 405.
- A failed save or any other unexpected error: 500 `internal error`. Nothing changes, and the server keeps running.

Paths are matched exactly, with no case folding, percent-decoding or slash normalisation. The query string is ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`.

### `POST /api/bookings` validation

The body needs `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`. Any other keys are ignored. The rules are checked in this order, and the first rule that fails decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Reply |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type must be `application/json` (letter case is ignored, and parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` are allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | The body must be at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | The body must be a JSON object | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` must be exactly one of the room names | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` must be a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming (the trimmed title is stored) | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD` and a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` must be later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | The booking must not overlap another booking of the same room on the same date. Back-to-back bookings are allowed. | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the times of the earliest overlapping booking) |

Only `title` is trimmed. Values such as ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are rejected.

Example:

```sh
curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
```

## Tests

```sh
npm test             # runs: node --test
```

The tests use `node:test` and live in `test/`. The server tests start `node server.mjs` with `PORT=0` and a temporary data file.

## Data file layout
```json

```

  integer < nextId and unique; title already trimmed (1-80 code units); room/date/
  start/end valid by the spec rules; start < end; no two same-room same-date overlaps.
- Anything else (empty file, invalid JSON, extra keys, ...) -> stderr
  `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` and exit 1. ENOENT -> `{nextId:1,bookings:[]}`.
- Written with `JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) + "\n"` directly to the path (no temp
  file, no mkdir), only on successful POST/DELETE, before the reply.
- Test tip: a fresh empty state on disk is `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}`.

## Page files
- `GET /` -> `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
  `GET /app.js` -> `public/app.js` (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`).

- Read from disk on every request (no cache); a read failure -> 500 `internal error` JSON.

## Concurrency
- Every request's body is read fully first (only the first 10000 bytes are kept; all
  bytes are counted for 413), then routing + handling run through one FIFO queue, so

## stdout / stderr
- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. Bad PORT / bind error: one
  stderr line, exit code 1.

content.content: # Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02 AUTOMATED BENCHMARK TASK. No human will answer questions: the requirements below are complete and final. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. The project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `` is the last element in body. ## app.js runtime contract (for the node:vm fake DOM) - Classic script wrapped in an IIFE; needs only globals `document` and `fetch`. - Browser APIs used, and nothing else: - `fetch(url, { method, headers?, body? })` — every call passes an options object (`{ method: 'GET' }` for GETs). Reply: `status`, `json()` only. `json()` is never called on a 204. - `document.getElementById`, `document.createElement` (`option`, `li`, `button`). - Element members: `textContent`, `value`, `type`, `disabled`, `append`, `replaceChildren`, `addEventListener`. Event: `preventDefault`. - Text nodes are made with `li.append(string)` (no createTextNode): a fake `append` must accept strings as text-node children. - `#room` filled via `replaceChildren(...options)`; list via `replaceChildren(...lis)`. - Each booking `li` gets `append(text)` then `append(button)`. - Listeners: form `submit`, `#filter-date` `change`, `#show-all` `click`, each Cancel button `click`. Handlers ignore the event object except submit (`preventDefault`). - Startup order: `GET /api/rooms` then `GET /api/bookings` (both before any reply). - Cancel and Book both ignore a trigger while their button is disabled. - Malformed 200 body (rooms/bookings not an array) shows `Request failed.`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Swaps each near-miss copy into place, runs npm test, records pass/fail, ALWAYS restores originals.
set -u
ROOT=/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23
BACKUP=$ROOT/.team/scratch/testing-orig
mkdir -p "$BACKUP"
cp "$ROOT/server.mjs" "$BACKUP/server.mjs"
cp "$ROOT/public/app.js" "$BACKUP/app.js"
restore() {
  cp "$BACKUP/server.mjs" "$ROOT/server.mjs"
  cp "$BACKUP/app.js" "$ROOT/public/app.js"
}
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

for copy in $(ls "$ROOT/.team/near-miss/" | sort -n); do
  case "$copy" in
    *-server.mjs) target="$ROOT/server.mjs" ;;
    *-app.js) target="$ROOT/public/app.js" ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac
  cp "$ROOT/.team/near-miss/$copy" "$target"
  fails=$(cd "$ROOT" && npm test 2>&1 | grep -E '^# fail ' | awk '{print $3}')
  restore
  if [ "${fails:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then echo "CAUGHT  $copy ($fails failing)"; else echo "MISSED  $copy"; fi
done
restore
diff -q "$BACKUP/server.mjs" "$ROOT/server.mjs" && diff -q "$BACKUP/app.js" "$ROOT/public/app.js" && echo "originals restored"

summary:
The suite fails this job's bar. The main reason is copy-pasted helpers across the test files. The second is one real gap: no test catches the browser script treating any 2xx reply as success.

**What I checked:** all 12 files listed, read in full against `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md`. I also ran `npm test`: 474 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, about 6 s. I tried to look for the `res.ok` gap in `.team/near-miss/` with a shell command, which was denied. A file search confirmed no test covers it.

**What is good**
- Spec messages are compared exactly as `{ error: message }`, with the exact Content-Type.
- Edge cases sit right at the limits: 10000 vs 10001 bytes (plain, multi-byte and chunked), titles of 80 vs 81 characters (including emoji), leap years, 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, and touching bookings.
- The order of the booking rules is tested as a ladder (each case breaks every later rule too).
- Some tests target specific wrong implementations: the earliest-starting overlap is named rather than the first created, `trim` is used rather than `trimEnd`, and ids are not used up by failed POSTs.
- The fake browser records any API the spec does not allow.
- Temp folders and server processes are always cleaned up in `finally`/`after`, and every startup and exit has a time limit.

**What needs fixing**

1. **Duplication (the main failure).**
   - The same error-check function is written five times:
     - `api-routing.test.mjs:10`
     - `api-bookings-list.test.mjs:9`
     - `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:57`
     - `api-booking-fields.test.mjs:45`
     - `server-persistence.test.mjs:39` (as `assertError`)
   - About 50 lines are copied between `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:8-71` and `api-booking-fields.test.mjs:8-59`: `SIX_KEYS`, `MSG`, `dayCounter`/`freshDate`, `booking`, `label`, `useServer`, `assertCreated`.
   - Other repeats: `listBookings`, the temp-folder-plus-server wrappers, the server setup/teardown in `api-routing` and `api-bookings-list`, and `assertOnlyAllowedApis`.
   - `postWith` (`api-booking-rules.test.mjs:33`) repeats what `postBooking`'s `contentType` option already does.

2. **Missing test: "error status" means "not the exact success status".** Every error case uses 4xx or 5xx. A script using `res.ok` or `status >= 400` would pass the whole suite.

3. **Smaller gaps.**
   - The Cancel 404/500 test never checks that the button is enabled again.
   - Label, h1 and button text is compared after `.trim()`, which is looser than the "exactly this text" the spec gives.

4. **Possible flakiness.** `freePort()` frees a port and reuses it later, which can race with other processes. The port-3000 test checks the port, then binds it, and skips itself if it is busy.

5. **Readability.** The title cases contain invisible Unicode characters (NBSP, U+3000, BOM, U+2028/2029, zero-width space). `JSON.stringify` keeps most of them invisible, so several tests end up with identical names such as `accepts " x "`.

## GRADE
Overall: 8.1/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — helpers are well split, but each file sets up its own server and has its own module-level `dayCounter` state
naming: 7 — `api-booking-rules` and `api-booking-fields` both cover booking rules (1-5 vs 6-10), short names (`r`, `s`, `ls`, `fd`, `lis`), several tests share the same name
duplication: 5 — the error check is copied 5 times; about 50 lines of helpers are copied between the two booking-rule files; `postWith` repeats `postBooking`
size: 9 — every file is under 300 lines and every function is well under 50
errors: 8 — time limits and kill/cleanup in `finally`, but `exists()` swallows every error and an empty error handler has no comment
tests: 8 — exact spec values and strong limit cases, but no 2xx-but-wrong-status case, the Cancel error test does not check the button is enabled again, `.trim()` loosens exact text checks, port races
security: 10 — no secrets; child process gets a cleaned environment; temp folders only
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs
Fixes:
- test/api-routing.test.mjs:10, test/api-bookings-list.test.mjs:9, test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:57, test/api-booking-fields.test.mjs:45, test/server-persistence.test.mjs:39 move the error check into test/helpers/server-harness.mjs as `assertJsonError` and import it
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:8-71 and test/api-booking-fields.test.mjs:8-59 move SIX_KEYS, MSG, freshDate, booking, label, useServer and assertCreated into a shared helper (e.g. test/helpers/booking-api.mjs); keep one date counter per process
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:33 delete `postWith`; use `postBooking(port, value, { contentType, raw })`, which already sends no header for `contentType: undefined`
- test/api-routing.test.mjs:26, test/server-persistence.test.mjs:33 share one `listBookings`; share the temp-folder-plus-server wrappers (server-startup.test.mjs:16-33, server-persistence.test.mjs:13-27) and the server setup/teardown (api-routing.test.mjs:37-46, api-bookings-list.test.mjs:53-62) through the harness
- test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:7, test/app-actions.test.mjs:5 export `assertOnlyAllowedApis` from test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs
- test/app-actions.test.mjs:117 add cases where a POST gets 200 and a DELETE gets 200 with `{error:'x'}`, and test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:60 add a rooms/list fetch that gets 201 or 204; each must show the error, so that `res.ok` / `status >= 400` fail
- test/app-actions.test.mjs:191-199 assert `button.disabled === false` after a Cancel 404/500
- test/page-html.test.mjs:41,44,77,85,97 compare text without `.trim()`, or only remove the whitespace the page's own markup adds, so `Room ` or ` Book` text would fail
- test/server-startup.test.mjs:132-138 drop the free-then-reuse `freePort()` race (e.g. retry on EADDRINUSE, or test the leading zero with `PORT=00` plus the existing `00000` case)
- test/server-startup.test.mjs:115-116 the check-then-bind of port 3000 races, and the test silently skips; note this or make the skip reason visible in CI
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:244,256-260 write the invisible characters as `\u00a0`, `\u3000\ufeff`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`, `\u200b` and give each case a unique test name
- test/server-persistence.test.mjs:30 only return false on `err.code === 'ENOENT'` and rethrow anything else
- test/server-persistence.test.mjs:229 comment that the empty error handler is there on purpose (the abort is what the test does)
- test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:96 use `instanceof TextNode` (exported from fake-dom) instead of `constructor.name`

A Cancel click while that button is disabled sends nothing (matches browser behaviour; same guard as Book). A 200 list/rooms reply without an array shows `Request failed.` instead of throwing.

"Error status" means any status other than the request's exact success status (200/201/204), so tests also send 200 to a POST, 201/204 to GETs and 200/201 to a DELETE. content.content:
1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app. `server.mjs` is one HTTP server that serves a JSON API and a browser page. You can book three fixed rooms (`Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`) by date and time, list and filter bookings, and cancel them. All data is kept in one JSON file.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	- Node.js (a version with `node:test`, 18 or later).
8	- No dependencies. You do not need to run `npm install`.
9	
10	## Usage
11	
12	```sh
13	npm start            # same as: node server.mjs
14	```
15	
16	The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is ready it prints one line to stdout:
17	
18	```
19	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
20	```
21	
22	Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a browser (use the port from that line).
23	
24	### Environment variables
25	
26	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
27	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
28	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means 3000. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick any free port, and the startup line shows which one. It must be ASCII digits only and no more than 65535. |
29	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |
30	
31	Example:
32	
33	```sh
34	PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=data/b.json node server.mjs
35	```
36	
37	The server never creates folders, so `data/` must already exist. If it does not, the server still starts, but every booking or cancel fails with `500 internal error`.
38	
39	On startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening. If `PORT` is invalid or the port cannot be bound (for example because it is already in use), the server writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1.
40	
41	## Data file
42	
43	- The file holds `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [...]}`.
44	- It is read once, at startup:
45	  - If it does not exist, the server starts with no bookings.
46	  - If it cannot be read for any other reason (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not valid data, the server prints `cannot read data file <name>` to stderr and exits with code 1.
47	- After startup the server's memory is the source of truth. Edits made to the file while the server runs are not noticed.
48	- The file is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and always before the reply is sent. After a restart you get the same bookings and the same next id.
49	- Ids start at 1 and are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
50	
51	## API
52	
53	Every JSON reply has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": "<message>"}`.
54	
55	A booking looks like this:
56	
57	```json
58	{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
59	```
60	
61	| Method & path | Success | Errors |
62	|---------------|---------|--------|
63	| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
64	| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above) | |
65	| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200, with only the bookings on that date | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` (an empty value counts as invalid) |
66	| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 with the new booking | see the validation rules below |
67	| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found` (the id is unknown, or is not a positive integer without a leading zero) |
68	| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
69	| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |
70	
71	Errors that apply to every route:
72	
73	- Any other path: 404 `not found`. This includes `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`.
74	- A known path with a method it does not support (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example, `GET /api/bookings/abc` returns 405.
75	- A failed save or any other unexpected error: 500 `internal error`. Nothing changes, and the server keeps running.
76	
77	Paths are matched exactly, with no case folding, percent-decoding or slash normalisation. The query string is ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`.
78	
79	### `POST /api/bookings` validation
80	
81	The body needs `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`. Any other keys are ignored. The rules are checked in this order, and the first rule that fails decides the reply:
82	
83	| # | Rule | Reply |
84	|---|------|-------|
85	| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type must be `application/json` (letter case is ignored, and parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` are allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
86	| 2 | The body must be at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
87	| 3 | The body must be a JSON object | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
88	| 4 | `room` must be exactly one of the room names | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
89	| 5 | `title` must be a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming (the trimmed title is stored) | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
90	| 6 | `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD` and a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
91	| 7 | `start` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
92	| 8 | `end` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
93	| 9 | `end` must be later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
94	| 10 | The booking must not overlap another booking of the same room on the same date. Back-to-back bookings are allowed. | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the times of the earliest overlapping booking) |
95	
96	Only `title` is trimmed. Values such as ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are rejected.
97	
98	Example:
99	
100	```sh
101	curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
102	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
103	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
104	```
105	
106	## Tests
107	
108	```sh
109	npm test             # runs: node --test
110	```
111	
112	The tests use `node:test` and live in `test/`. The server tests start `node server.mjs` with `PORT=0` and a temporary data file.
113

I graded `server.mjs`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `README.md` and `package.json` against every line of `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md`. **Verdict: pass, 9.3/10.** I found no confirmed spec violations and no request that can crash the server. `npm test` passes: 485/485 tests, 0 failing. I was not allowed to run my own live tests against the server, so the two edge cases below come from reading the code and how Node 22 behaves.

**Spec check, server (`/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs`)**
- **Startup:**
  - Startup runs in the right order: PORT, then data file, then listen.
  - `PORT` must be all ASCII digits and at most 65535. Leading zeros are accepted, which the spec allows.
  - Exactly one line goes to stdout: `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` using the port actually bound.
  - `DATA_FILE` is resolved against the current folder, and the error message uses the name as given.
  - ENOENT means no bookings yet. Any other read error, including ENOTDIR and EISDIR, gives the exact `cannot read data file <name>\n` and exit 1.
- **Data-file check against what the server writes:**
  - The server writes `{nextId, bookings}`. Each booking has exactly 6 keys, a trimmed title, `id < nextId`, unique ids and no overlaps, because POST already enforces all of that.
  - A lone surrogate or U+2028 in a title is escaped by `JSON.stringify` and reads back the same.
  - So the strict check never rejects a file the server wrote itself.
- **Writes:**
  - The only write is `store.commit`, and it is called only on a POST that passes every rule or a DELETE that finds the booking.
  - Memory changes only after the save succeeds, so a failed save changes nothing, including the next id.
- **Booking rules:**
  - The 10 rules run in spec order, with 415 checked before 413.
  - The 413 count includes every byte received, not the `Content-Length` header.
  - The body is decoded with `toString('utf8')`, so a byte order mark is kept.
  - The date and time patterns use ASCII-only `[0-9]` and `$` (which matches only at the true end of the string). Leap years are `% 4`.
  - Overlap uses `b.start < end && start < b.end`, and the 409 message names the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- **Routes:**
  - Paths are compared byte for byte.
  - `?date` with no `=` gets 400.
  - The DELETE id must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`.
  - HEAD and OPTIONS get 405. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` get 404.
  - The JSON `Content-Type`, the page and script `Content-Type` values, and every message string are exact.
- **Robustness:**
  - The whole body is read before any reply, outside the queue, so a slow upload cannot block other requests.
  - An aborted body ends with `req.destroy()`.
  - A throw after headers are sent ends with `res.destroy()`.
  - The queue's tail always settles, so one failure cannot jam it.
  - Nothing in the error path can throw, so there are no unhandled rejections.

**Spec check, page and script (`public/index.html`, `public/app.js`)**
- The page's elements, attributes, label texts and empty `#error` are correct. It has no `<option>`, no room names and no `http(s)://`, and the `<script src="/app.js">` is the last element in `<body>`.
- The script uses only the allowed browser APIs.
- Error status means anything other than exactly 200, 201 or 204. A non-204 reply whose body is not JSON counts as no reply.
- The rooms and list requests both start at load.
- The list uses a sequence counter so only the last fetch started counts, and a successful list leaves `#error` alone. `?date=` is added unencoded.
- `Book` is re-enabled right after the request settles.
- Cancel with no reply does not refetch the list. `Show all` sets the value without dispatching an event.

**README and package.json**
- Scripts, environment variables, data layout, the `test/` location, the API table and the messages all match the code. Two small wording gaps are in the fix list.

**Fix list**
1. **Edge-case spec risk (no crash)**, `server.mjs:338`: a `CONNECT /api/rooms` request gets no reply. With no `'connect'` listener, Node 22 drops the connection, but the stricter reading of spec line 30 wants 405. Fix: add `server.on('connect', ...)` that writes a 405 (or 404) JSON reply on the socket and closes it.
2. **Edge-case spec risk (no crash)**, `server.mjs:338`: a request with an `Expect` value other than `100-continue` gets Node's automatic 417. It skips the route handler and does not read the body (spec line 17). Fix: add a `server.on('checkExpectation', listener)` that sends these requests through the normal request handler.
3. **Quality nit**, `server.mjs:127`: the save overwrites the file in place. If the disk fills up or a write fails partway, the file can be cut short. The server's memory stays right, but the next startup would refuse the file. Writing to a temporary file in the same folder and renaming it avoids this, and creates no folders.
4. **Quality nit**, `public/app.js:68-84` and `118-139`: `loadRooms` and `loadList` repeat the same handling for no reply, error status and unexpected body. One helper could do this.
5. **README nit**, `README.md:37`: "every booking or cancel fails with 500" is too broad. Only successful creates and deletes fail; cancelling an unknown id still gives 404.
6. **README nit**, `README.md:46`: say that `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` exactly as given (`bookings.json` when unset).

## GRADE
Overall: 9.3/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — small single-purpose functions, nesting depth at most 3, state replaced with new objects, queue and store cleanly separated
naming: 9 — clear names (`parseBookingRequest`, `isBookingItemPath`, `createQueue`), `MSG` table matches the spec text
duplication: 9 — only the repeated reply handling in app.js `loadRooms`/`loadList`
size: 10 — server.mjs 349, app.js 203, index.html 42 lines; every function under 50 lines
errors: 8 — every failure ends as one line or a 500 with no stack trace, but CONNECT gets no reply, a non-100 Expect skips the body read, and the in-place save can leave a cut-short file
tests: n/a — written by the testing section (485/485 pass)
security: 10 — no secrets, all values shown with textContent/append, paths compared exactly, no user input reaches file paths
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or commented-out code; stderr diagnostics are deliberate
Fixes:
- server.mjs:338 Edge-case spec risk: add a `'connect'` listener that replies 405/404 JSON instead of letting Node drop the connection
- server.mjs:338 Edge-case spec risk: add a `'checkExpectation'` listener that runs the normal handler so the body is read and the route's reply is sent
- server.mjs:127 Quality nit: write to a temp file in the same folder and rename, so a failed save cannot cut the data file short
- public/app.js:68 Quality nit: merge the shared reply handling of `loadRooms`/`loadList` into one helper
- README.md:37 Quality nit: say only successful creates/deletes fail with 500 when the folder is missing

**Verdict: pass.** The final review found two real spec violations in server.mjs. Backend fixed both, and I re-verified them. The whole app now matches the spec, with no crash paths found.

**Final review (reviewer, 9.3/10, no item under 8).** I checked server.mjs, public/index.html, public/app.js, README.md and package.json against the spec line by line. README.md matches the code: the scripts, environment variables, the `{"nextId","bookings"}` data layout, the `test/` folder, the API table and the messages. The data-file check never rejects a file the server wrote itself.

**Crash paths (probed live).** None crashed the server or wrote to stderr, and it kept answering afterwards:
- a client aborting mid-body (fixed length and chunked);
- a garbage request line;
- `OPTIONS *` and `GET *`, which get 404;
- absolute-form targets, which get 404 because the path isn't byte-equal to a route;
- pipelined requests and HTTP/1.0;
- `__proto__` and `constructor` keys in the body, `/__proto__` as a path, and deeply nested JSON.

**The two violations (fixed and re-verified):**
1. **CONNECT got no reply at all.** Node dropped the connection. Now `CONNECT /api/rooms` gets 405 `method not allowed`, and a CONNECT to any other target gets 404 `not found`.
2. **An unknown `Expect` header got Node's automatic 417.** The route never ran and the body was never read. Now such a request gets its normal reply (415 in the test).

I wrote the failing tests first in `test/server-edge-requests.test.mjs`, sent them to backend, and reviewed backend's diff. The suite is now 489/489. I rebuilt the near-miss copies from the new server.mjs and re-ran the 16 server copies (app.js didn't change). All 22 still fail the suite, and both originals are restored byte-identical.
